Package hadur2.core.shieldmode

Class ShieldGeometry

java.lang.Object
hadur2.core.shieldmode.ShieldGeometry
public final class ShieldGeometry extends Object
Where to fire so that our bullet meets an enemy bullet in mid-air (SHIELD-5).

The engine moves every bullet once per turn and destroys two bullets whose paths for that turn cross. A bullet fired in the tick t code leaves from where the robot stood at that tick and ends turn k at distance speed * (k - t). So in turn k our bullet sweeps a ring around the firing point, and it meets the enemy bullet if it crosses the part of the enemy bullet's path for that turn that lies inside the ring. That part, seen from the firing point, is an angular interval: the "shadow". Firing at its middle meets the bullet with the most room for error.

The engine checks robot hits before bullet hits, so the meeting has to happen before the enemy bullet can first touch our body. If the firing point lies on the enemy bullet's line the paths are collinear and never cross, which is why the shield steps aside first.
